alphabeta.source_excerpt: Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, $A$ its Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ the standard projection and $P=\ker\pi$. For a subset $J\subseteq S$, let $W_J$ and $A_J$ be the standard parabolic subgroups. Write $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$, $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$, and let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$. Then $\pi$ induces $\overline\pi:N(A,J)\to N(W,J)$ and the sequence $1\to N(P,J)\to N(A,J)\xrightarrow{\overline\pi}N(W,J)\to1$ is exact. Here exactness means that the inclusion $N(P,J)\hookrightarrow N(A,J)$ is injective, its image equals $\ker\overline\pi$, and $\overline\pi$ is surjective.

alphabeta.original_label: Normalisers and their quotients
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system indexed by $S=\{s_i:i\in\Gamma_0\}$, let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group, and let $P=\ker(\pi:A\to W)$ be its pure Artin–Tits group. For $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$, let $W_J=\langle s_j:j\in J\rangle$ and $A_J=\langle\sigma_j:j\in J\rangle$ be the standard parabolic subgroups; the brackets denote the subgroups generated by the displayed elements.

For $G=W$ with $G_J=W_J$, or $G=A$ with $G_J=A_J$, define the **normaliser** of $G_J$ in $G$ by $\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)=\{g\in G:gG_Jg^{-1}=G_J\}$. Define the normaliser quotient groups $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$.

Define $N(P,J)=\{\beta A_J\in N(A,J):P\cap\beta A_J\ne\varnothing\}$. Equivalently, $N(P,J)$ is the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ under the quotient homomorphism $\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)\to N(A,J)$.

Proof. Note that XJ  is a complexified hyperplane complement from a real, central (since the
hyperplanes are linear) finite hyperplane arrangement in a vector space (recall that we are in
spherical-type). Moreover, the chambers of the real arrangement are open simplicial cones. There-

fore Deligne’s Theorem [9] applies, and XJ  is a K(π, 1). Since X J →X J /N(W, J) is a normal
                                      C
cover (see paragraph before (3.28)) and π1(X J /N(W, J), x) ∼= N(A, J) by Theorem 6.7, the result
follows.                                                  □

alphabeta.original_label: Spherical relative arrangements and Deligne topology
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, let $J\subseteq S$, and use its relative space $\Theta_J$, relative cone $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$, relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$, positive arrangement category $\mathcal D^+(J)$ and groupoid completion $\mathcal D(J)$. Suppose $W$ is finite, also called spherical type. Then $\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ=\Theta_J$, and $(\Theta_J,\mathcal H^J)$ is a finite central simplicial arrangement: its hyperplanes are finite in number, pass through the origin, and each chamber is a linear image of an open positive orthant in $\Theta_J$.

The category $\mathcal D^+(J)$ has a finite-type atomic categorical Garside structure. Thus its completion $\mathcal D(J)$ is a Garside groupoid in the sense of being the groupoid completion of that Garside category. It is equivalent to the fundamental groupoid $\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C})$ of the relative complexified complement. These deductions use the finite simplicial hypotheses; no extension to a general nonsimplicial or infinite arrangement is asserted.

We now provide the construction of such an equivalence. For each chamber C in (Cone(J)◦, HJ),
define
                                 C
             XC := {x + iy ∈XJ  | ∀H ∈HJ, x ∈H ⇒y ∈DH(C)},
where DH(C) denotes the half space delimited by H in which C is included. The set XC is open
    C
in XJ and is contractible by [30, Corollary I.2.18]. Let C, C′ be two adjacent chambers separated
by a hyperplane H0. By [30, Corollary I.2.19], the intersection XC ∩XC′ admits two connected
components, given by
                       C
      XC,C′ – {x + iy ∈XJ  | x ∈DH0(C) and ∀H ∈HJ, x ∈H ⇒y ∈DH(C) = DH(C′)},
and XC′,C, which is defined by swapping the roles of C and C′ above. Define a functor p : D →
    C
π1(X J ) as follows.  Firstly, choose for each chamber C a point aC ∈XC in such a way that
ag·C = g · aC. This defines p on objects, sending C 7→aC. For adjacent chambers C and C′, the
image of the one-step path C →C′ in D under p is defined as follow. Choose a point d ∈XC,C′
and let γ1 (resp. γ2) be a path in XC (resp. in XC′) from aC to d (resp. from d to aC′). The
                                          C
concatenation γ1γ2 is a path from aC to aC′ in XJ , whose homotopy class depends only on the
connected component XC,C′ (and does not depend on the choice of γ1, γ2, d); see discussion after
[30, Definition I.1.3]. The image of the one-step path C →C′ in D under p is defined as the

--- PDF PAGE 26 ---
26          OWEN GARNIER, EDMUND HENG, ANTHONY LICATA, AND ODED YACOBI

homotopy class of γ1γ2.1 By [30, Theorem I.4.10], p is well-defined and is an equivalence from
         C
D to π1(X J ).  Since g · XC,C′ = Xg·C,g·C′ for all g ∈N(W, J), it follows immediately from the
construction that p is N(W, J)-equivariant.                              □

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, let $J\subseteq S$, and put $G=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$, where $W_J$ is generated by $J$. Use the relative real space $E$, its finite hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal H^J$, and its complexified complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ from [def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers). A chamber is a connected component of $E\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}H$; two chambers are adjacent if they share a wall. For each chamber $C$ use its open set $X_C$, and for an ordered adjacent pair $(C,C')$ use the specified component $X_{C,C'}\subseteq X_C\cap X_{C'}$, as defined in [def-chamber-open-sets-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-chamber-open-sets-artin-tits-normalisers).

Choose points $a_C\in X_C$ satisfying $a_{gC}=g a_C$ for every $g\in G$. Assign $C$ to $a_C$. alphabeta.original_label: Deligne-to-ribbon functor is a covering
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Let $\mathcal D^+(J)$ be the positive category of the relative chamber arrangement and $\mathcal D(J)$ its groupoid completion. Let $\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid and $\mathcal G:\mathcal D(J)\to\mathcal R(J)$ the functor sending a chamber label $(x,I)$ to $I$ and a simple crossing with index $a\notin I$ to the elementary ribbon $\mu_{a,I}$.

The functor $\mathcal G$ is a groupoid covering: for every chamber $C$ and every arrow of $\mathcal R(J)$ with source $\mathcal G(C)$, there is exactly one arrow of $\mathcal D(J)$ with source $C$ and that image. Each elementary ribbon lifts from $(x,I)$ to the corresponding simple wall crossing. The two sides of each defining ribbon-lcm relation lift from a fixed source chamber to equal morphisms of $\mathcal D^+(J)$.

alphabeta.original_label: Reduced ribbon groupoid is the Deligne orbit quotient
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Write $W_I$ for the subgroup generated by $I\subseteq S$, and let $N=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$. Let $\mathcal D$ be the relative arrangement groupoid, whose objects are chamber labels $(x,I)$, and let $\mathcal R$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid. Its objects are the associates of $J$: the subsets $I\subseteq S$ for which $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$. The functor $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ sends $(x,I)$ to $I$ and a simple wall crossing of index $a$ to the elementary ribbon $\mu_{a,I}$. Let $\mathcal Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/N$ send objects and arrows to their orbits under the normaliser action.

The functor $\mathcal G$ factors as $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'\circ\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal G':\mathcal D/N\to\mathcal R$ is an isomorphism of groupoids. On objects it identifies the $N$-orbits of chambers with the associates of $J$ by $[(x,I)]\mapsto I$.

alphabeta.original_label: Equivariant equivalence with fundamental groupoids
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Put $G=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$, where $W_J$ is generated by $J$. Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified arrangement complement and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(J)$ be the groupoid completion of the positive relative chamber category. Thus its objects are chambers and its generating arrows are directed crossings of adjacent chambers, subject to equality of positive geodesic galleries with the same endpoints and formal inversion of arrows.

The space $X$ is nonempty, path-connected and locally path-connected.

There is a $G$-equivariant equivalence $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$, where $\Pi_1(X)$ has points of $X$ as objects and endpoint-fixed path-homotopy classes as arrows. Equivariance means $p(gC)=g p(C)$ on objects and $p(g\alpha)=g p(\alpha)$ on arrows. With $Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/G$ the orbit functor and $q:X\to X/G$ the topological orbit map, $p$ induces an equivalence $\bar p:\mathcal D/G\to\Pi_1(X/G)$ satisfying $\bar p\,Q=q_*p$. The map $q$ is a normal covering. An equivalence means a functor equipped with a quasi-inverse and natural isomorphisms to the two identity functors; the Axiom of Choice is used below to choose connecting paths for all objects.

alphabeta.original_label: Equivariant equivalence with fundamental groupoids
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Put $G=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$, where $W_J$ is generated by $J$. Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified arrangement complement and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(J)$ be the groupoid completion of the positive relative chamber category. Thus its objects are chambers and its generating arrows are directed crossings of adjacent chambers, subject to equality of positive geodesic galleries with the same endpoints and formal inversion of arrows.

The space $X$ is nonempty, path-connected and locally path-connected.

There is a $G$-equivariant equivalence $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$, where $\Pi_1(X)$ has points of $X$ as objects and endpoint-fixed path-homotopy classes as arrows. Equivariance means $p(gC)=g p(C)$ on objects and $p(g\alpha)=g p(\alpha)$ on arrows. With $Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/G$ the orbit functor and $q:X\to X/G$ the topological orbit map, $p$ induces an equivalence $\bar p:\mathcal D/G\to\Pi_1(X/G)$ satisfying $\bar p\,Q=q_*p$. The map $q$ is a normal covering. An equivalence means a functor equipped with a quasi-inverse and natural isomorphisms to the two identity functors; the Axiom of Choice is used below to choose connecting paths for all objects.

alphabeta.original_label: Deligne-to-ribbon functor is a covering
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Let $\mathcal D^+(J)$ be the positive category of the relative chamber arrangement and $\mathcal D(J)$ its groupoid completion. Let $\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid and $\mathcal G:\mathcal D(J)\to\mathcal R(J)$ the functor sending a chamber label $(x,I)$ to $I$ and a simple crossing with index $a\notin I$ to the elementary ribbon $\mu_{a,I}$.

The functor $\mathcal G$ is a groupoid covering: for every chamber $C$ and every arrow of $\mathcal R(J)$ with source $\mathcal G(C)$, there is exactly one arrow of $\mathcal D(J)$ with source $C$ and that image. Each elementary ribbon lifts from $(x,I)$ to the corresponding simple wall crossing. The two sides of each defining ribbon-lcm relation lift from a fixed source chamber to equal morphisms of $\mathcal D^+(J)$.

alphabeta.original_label: Reduced ribbon groupoid is the Deligne orbit quotient
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Write $W_I$ for the subgroup generated by $I\subseteq S$, and let $N=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$. Let $\mathcal D$ be the relative arrangement groupoid, whose objects are chamber labels $(x,I)$, and let $\mathcal R$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid. Its objects are the associates of $J$: the subsets $I\subseteq S$ for which $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$. The functor $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ sends $(x,I)$ to $I$ and a simple wall crossing of index $a$ to the elementary ribbon $\mu_{a,I}$. Let $\mathcal Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/N$ send objects and arrows to their orbits under the normaliser action.

The functor $\mathcal G$ factors as $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'\circ\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal G':\mathcal D/N\to\mathcal R$ is an isomorphism of groupoids. On objects it identifies the $N$-orbits of chambers with the associates of $J$ by $[(x,I)]\mapsto I$.

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Use the finite-dimensional relative space $E=\Theta_J$, its finite set $\mathcal H^J$ of distinct linear hyperplanes, and the relative complexified complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ from [def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers). Thus $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ consists of $x+iy$ with $x,y\in E$ and no $H\in\mathcal H^J$ containing both $x$ and $y$. The arrangement has ambient domain $E$; its chambers are the connected components of $E\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}H$, and adjacent chambers are distinct chambers sharing a wall, as in [def-chambers-walls-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-chambers-walls-artin-tits-normalisers).

For $H\in\mathcal H^J$ and a chamber $C$, let $D_H(C)$ be the open half-space bounded by $H$ that contains $C$: if $a:E\to\mathbb R$ is a nonzero linear functional with kernel $H$, it is either $\{v:a(v)>0\}$ or $\{v:a(v)<0\}$, according to which contains $C$. Define

$$X_C=\{x+iy\in\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}:\text{ for every }H\in\mathcal H^J,\ x\in H\Rightarrow y\in D_H(C)\}.$$

Let $C,C'$ be adjacent, and let $H_0$ be their unique separating hyperplane. Define

$$X_{C,C'}=\{x+iy\in\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}:x\in D_{H_0}(C),\ \text{and for every }H\in\mathcal H^J,\ x\in H\Rightarrow y\in D_H(C)\cap D_H(C')\}.$$

Define $X_{C',C}$ by interchanging $C$ and $C'$ in this formula. These are subsets of $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ with its subspace topology.

define
                                 C
             XC := {x + iy ∈XJ  | ∀H ∈HJ, x ∈H ⇒y ∈DH(C)},
where DH(C) denotes the half space delimited by H in which C is included. The set XC is open
    C
in XJ and is contractible by [30, Corollary I.2.18]. Let C, C′ be two adjacent chambers separated
by a hyperplane H0. By [30, Corollary I.2.19], the intersection XC ∩XC′ admits two connected
components, given by
                       C
      XC,C′ – {x + iy ∈XJ  | x ∈DH0(C) and ∀H ∈HJ, x ∈H ⇒y ∈DH(C) = DH(C′)},
and XC′,C, which is defined by swapping the roles of C and C′ above. Define a functor p : D →
    C
π1(X J ) as follows.  Firstly, choose for each chamber C a point aC ∈XC in such a way that
ag·C = g · aC. This defines p on objects, sending C 7→aC. For adjacent chambers C and C′, the
image of the one-step path C →C′ in D under p is defined as follow. Choose a point d ∈XC,C′
and let γ1 (resp. γ2) be a path in XC (resp. in XC′) from aC to d (resp. from d to aC′). The
                                          C
concatenation γ1γ2 is a path from aC to aC′ in XJ , whose homotopy class depends only on the
connected component XC,C′ (and does not depend on the choice of γ1, γ2, d); see discussion after
[30, Definition I.1.3]. The image of the one-step path C →C′ in D under p is defined as the

alphabeta.original_label: Contractibility and intersection components of chamber open sets
alphabeta.source_excerpt: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Use the relative real space $E$, its finite hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal H^J$, its complexified complement, and the chamber sets $X_C$, $X_{C,C'}$ and $X_{C',C}$ of the chamber-set definition. A chamber is a connected component of the real arrangement complement; adjacent chambers share a wall. Then $X_C$ is open and contractible. If $C$ and $C'$ are adjacent, $X_C\cap X_{C'}$ has exactly two connected components, namely $X_{C,C'}$ and $X_{C',C}$.

article.source_excerpt:
Theorem 3.9 ([24, Theorem 1.15]). Let Γ be a Coxeter diagram with associated Coxeter group
W, and let J be a subset of the vertex set Γ0. There is a bijection between the set of chambers of
(Cone(J)◦, HJ) and the following set

           Cham(J) – {(x, I) | WJx = xWI and x has minimal length in xWI},         (3.10)

--- PDF PAGE 10 ---
10          OWEN GARNIER, EDMUND HENG, ANTHONY LICATA, AND ODED YACOBI

given by sending (x, I) 7→x · CI.

alphabeta.original_label: Deligne-to-ribbon functor is a covering
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Let $\mathcal D^+(J)$ be the positive category of the relative chamber arrangement and $\mathcal D(J)$ its groupoid completion. Let $\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid and $\mathcal G:\mathcal D(J)\to\mathcal R(J)$ the functor sending a chamber label $(x,I)$ to $I$ and a simple crossing with index $a\notin I$ to the elementary ribbon $\mu_{a,I}$.

The functor $\mathcal G$ is a groupoid covering: for every chamber $C$ and every arrow of $\mathcal R(J)$ with source $\mathcal G(C)$, there is exactly one arrow of $\mathcal D(J)$ with source $C$ and that image. Each elementary ribbon lifts from $(x,I)$ to the corresponding simple wall crossing. The two sides of each defining ribbon-lcm relation lift from a fixed source chamber to equal morphisms of $\mathcal D^+(J)$.

alphabeta.original_label: Reduced ribbon groupoid is the Deligne orbit quotient
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Write $W_I$ for the subgroup generated by $I\subseteq S$, and let $N=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$. Let $\mathcal D$ be the relative arrangement groupoid, whose objects are chamber labels $(x,I)$, and let $\mathcal R$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid. Its objects are the associates of $J$: the subsets $I\subseteq S$ for which $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$. The functor $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ sends $(x,I)$ to $I$ and a simple wall crossing of index $a$ to the elementary ribbon $\mu_{a,I}$. Let $\mathcal Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/N$ send objects and arrows to their orbits under the normaliser action.

The functor $\mathcal G$ factors as $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'\circ\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal G':\mathcal D/N\to\mathcal R$ is an isomorphism of groupoids. On objects it identifies the $N$-orbits of chambers with the associates of $J$ by $[(x,I)]\mapsto I$.

alphabeta.original_label: Equivariant equivalence with fundamental groupoids
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Put $G=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$, where $W_J$ is generated by $J$. Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified arrangement complement and let $\mathcal D=\mathcal D(J)$ be the groupoid completion of the positive relative chamber category. Thus its objects are chambers and its generating arrows are directed crossings of adjacent chambers, subject to equality of positive geodesic galleries with the same endpoints and formal inversion of arrows.

The space $X$ is nonempty, path-connected and locally path-connected.

There is a $G$-equivariant equivalence $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$, where $\Pi_1(X)$ has points of $X$ as objects and endpoint-fixed path-homotopy classes as arrows. Equivariance means $p(gC)=g p(C)$ on objects and $p(g\alpha)=g p(\alpha)$ on arrows. With $Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/G$ the orbit functor and $q:X\to X/G$ the topological orbit map, $p$ induces an equivalence $\bar p:\mathcal D/G\to\Pi_1(X/G)$ satisfying $\bar p\,Q=q_*p$. The map $q$ is a normal covering. An equivalence means a functor equipped with a quasi-inverse and natural isomorphisms to the two identity functors; the Axiom of Choice is used below to choose connecting paths for all objects.

alphabeta.original_label: Geodesics are exactly length-additive wall words
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with vertex set $\Gamma_0$, and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. In its relative chamber arrangement, let $p=((x_1,I_1),\ldots,(x_m,I_m))$ be a nonempty chamber path. For each consecutive pair let $a_i$ be its crossing index and $v_{a_i,I_i}\in W$ its simple wall-crossing element. Put $v_p=v_{a_1,I_1}\cdots v_{a_{m-1},I_{m-1}}$, with the empty product equal to the identity. Write $\ell(w)$ for the least length of a word in the simple generators representing $w$.

The path $p$ is geodesic, meaning that its number of crossings is minimal among paths with the same endpoints, if and only if $\ell(v_p)=\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}\ell(v_{a_i,I_i})$. The empty sum is zero.

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Use the Coxeter-system notation of [def-coxeter-data-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-coxeter-data-artin-tits-normalisers): $\Gamma_0$ is the vertex set, $V=\bigoplus_{i\in\Gamma_0}\mathbb R\alpha_i$ has basis $(\alpha_i)_{i\in\Gamma_0}$, and $\Theta=V^*$ is the space of real linear functionals on $V$. The vertex set may be infinite.

For $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$, write $I^c=\Gamma_0\setminus I$. Define the parabolic coordinate subspace $\Theta_I$ and the fundamental face $C_I$ by $\Theta_I=\{\varphi\in\Theta:\varphi(\alpha_i)=0\text{ for every }i\in I\}$ and $C_I=\{\varphi\in\Theta_I:\varphi(\alpha_j)>0\text{ for every }j\in I^c\}$.

We now provide the construction of such an equivalence. For each chamber C in (Cone(J)◦, HJ),
define
                                 C
             XC := {x + iy ∈XJ  | ∀H ∈HJ, x ∈H ⇒y ∈DH(C)},
where DH(C) denotes the half space delimited by H in which C is included. The set XC is open
    C
in XJ and is contractible by [30, Corollary I.2.18]. Let C, C′ be two adjacent chambers separated
by a hyperplane H0. By [30, Corollary I.2.19], the intersection XC ∩XC′ admits two connected
components, given by
                       C
      XC,C′ – {x + iy ∈XJ  | x ∈DH0(C) and ∀H ∈HJ, x ∈H ⇒y ∈DH(C) = DH(C′)},
and XC′,C, which is defined by swapping the roles of C and C′ above. Define a functor p : D →
    C
π1(X J ) as follows.  Firstly, choose for each chamber C a point aC ∈XC in such a way that
ag·C = g · aC. This defines p on objects, sending C 7→aC. For adjacent chambers C and C′, the
image of the one-step path C →C′ in D under p is defined as follow. Choose a point d ∈XC,C′
and let γ1 (resp. γ2) be a path in XC (resp. in XC′) from aC to d (resp. from d to aC′). The
                                          C
concatenation γ1γ2 is a path from aC to aC′ in XJ , whose homotopy class depends only on the
connected component XC,C′ (and does not depend on the choice of γ1, γ2, d); see discussion after
[30, Definition I.1.3]. The image of the one-step path C →C′ in D under p is defined as the

homotopy class of γ1γ2.1 By [30, Theorem I.4.10], p is well-defined and is an equivalence from
         C
D to π1(X J ).  Since g · XC,C′ = Xg·C,g·C′ for all g ∈N(W, J), it follows immediately from the
construction that p is N(W, J)-equivariant.                              □

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $W$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Use the finite-dimensional relative space $E=\Theta_J$, its finite set $\mathcal H^J$ of distinct linear hyperplanes, and the relative complexified complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ from [def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers). Thus $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ consists of $x+iy$ with $x,y\in E$ and no $H\in\mathcal H^J$ containing both $x$ and $y$. The arrangement has ambient domain $E$; its chambers are the connected components of $E\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}H$, and adjacent chambers are distinct chambers sharing a wall, as in [def-chambers-walls-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-chambers-walls-artin-tits-normalisers).

For $H\in\mathcal H^J$ and a chamber $C$, let $D_H(C)$ be the open half-space bounded by $H$ that contains $C$: if $a:E\to\mathbb R$ is a nonzero linear functional with kernel $H$, it is either $\{v:a(v)>0\}$ or $\{v:a(v)<0\}$, according to which contains $C$. Define

article.original_label: Section 3.5, construction and finite simplicial specialization
article.source_excerpt:
3.5. The Deligne groupoid. The Deligne groupoid was introduced in [9] to study the topology
of finite simplicial arrangements (and prove the K(π, 1) conjecture for finite real reflection groups).
Although our setting is more general than that of Deligne, the construction of the Deligne groupoid
can be carried out similarly. However, the key features proven by Deligne, namely that the Deligne
groupoid is a Garside groupoid equivalent to the fundamental groupoid of the complexified com-
plement, only hold (to our knowledge) in the setting of finite simplicial arrangements.
  To the locally-finite arrangement (Cone(J)◦, HJ), we associate an oriented graph on the set
of vertices Cham(J). To every pair of adjacent chambers we associate a 2-cycle, i.e. given two
adjacent chambers (x, I) and (y, K) there is one arrow (x, I) →(y, K) and another opposite arrow
(y, K) →(x, I). We continue to use the notation ωa,I as above to label these arrows.
 A path in this graph from (x, I) to (y, K) is a geodesic if it is a path of minimal length between
(x, I) and (y, K). Equivalently, it crosses every hyperplane H ∈HJ at most once.
  Define D+ := D+(J) as the category with:
     • objects given by Cham(J); and

alphabeta.original_label: Deligne asphericity used for the relative complement
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let $\mathcal H$ be a finite collection of linear hyperplanes. Suppose every chamber, meaning every connected component of $V\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}H$, is an open simplicial cone: it is the image of an open positive orthant under a linear isomorphism onto $V$. Write $V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, with complex scalar multiplication $z\cdot(v\otimes w)=v\otimes zw$ and its finite-dimensional Euclidean topology. Then the complexified complement $M=V_{\mathbb C}\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}(H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$ is nonempty and path-connected, admits a CW structure, and has vanishing homotopy groups in all degrees at least two. Choose a vertex $b$ of such a CW structure and put $\pi=\pi_1(M,b)$. With the identity identification of this fundamental group with $\pi$, the based space $(M,b)$ is a $K(\pi,1)$. Here a $K(\pi,1)$ means a connected based CW complex with a specified fundamental-group isomorphism to $\pi$ and vanishing higher homotopy groups; the latter vanishing is called asphericity.

In particular, let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with $W$ finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. For its relative space $\Theta_J$, relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$ and relative complexified complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$, the space $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ admits a CW structure and, after choosing a vertex basepoint, is a $K(\pi,1)$ for its own fundamental group with the identity identification.

alphabeta.original_label: Spherical relative arrangements and Deligne topology
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, let $J\subseteq S$, and use its relative space $\Theta_J$, relative cone $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$, relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$, positive arrangement category $\mathcal D^+(J)$ and groupoid completion $\mathcal D(J)$. Suppose $W$ is finite, also called spherical type. Then $\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ=\Theta_J$, and $(\Theta_J,\mathcal H^J)$ is a finite central simplicial arrangement: its hyperplanes are finite in number, pass through the origin, and each chamber is a linear image of an open positive orthant in $\Theta_J$.

The category $\mathcal D^+(J)$ has a finite-type atomic categorical Garside structure. Thus its completion $\mathcal D(J)$ is a Garside groupoid in the sense of being the groupoid completion of that Garside category. It is equivalent to the fundamental groupoid $\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C})$ of the relative complexified complement. These deductions use the finite simplicial hypotheses; no extension to a general nonsimplicial or infinite arrangement is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group and $P$ the kernel of its standard projection to $W$. For $G=W,A$, let $G_J$ be the standard parabolic subgroup generated by the generators indexed by $J$, and put $N(G,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)/G_J$, where the normaliser consists of the elements conjugating $G_J$ to itself. Let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$.

Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified hyperplane complement. The induced action of $N(W,J)$ gives a quotient $X/N(W,J)$. Then $X$ is a $K(N(P,J),1)$ and $X/N(W,J)$ is a $K(N(A,J),1)$. Here $K(G,1)$ means a path-connected space whose fundamental group is isomorphic to $G$ and whose homotopy groups in all degrees at least two vanish.

alphabeta.original_label: Main spherical theorem combining exact sequences and asphericity
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $S$ is finite and $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ its standard projection, and $P=\ker\pi$. For $G=W,A$, let $G_J$ be the subgroup generated by the standard generators indexed by $J$, and define $N(G,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)/G_J$, where $\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)=\{g\in G:gG_Jg^{-1}=G_J\}$. Let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$.

Let $\Theta_J$ be the subspace of the real dual reflection representation on which the simple roots indexed by $J$ vanish, and let $\mathcal H^J$ consist of the distinct hyperplanes obtained by restricting to $\Theta_J$ those root hyperplanes that do not contain it. In spherical type, the relative complexified complement is $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}=(\Theta_J\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}(H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$, with its subspace topology. The action of $N(W,J)$ on $X$ is the complex-linear extension of $(nW_J)\cdot f=nf$, where $(nf)(v)=f(n^{-1}v)$ for $f\in\Theta_J$, $v$ in the real root space and $n\in\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)$. It is independent of the representative and preserves $X$. For $x\in X$, let $\bar x$ be its image in $X/N(W,J)$ under this action.

The algebraic exact sequence $1\to N(P,J)\to N(A,J)\to N(W,J)\to1$ is isomorphic to the covering exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)\to N(W,J)\to1$, with the identity on $N(W,J)$. In particular, $N(P,J)\cong\pi_1(X,x)$ and $N(A,J)\cong\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)$. Moreover, $X$ is a $K(N(P,J),1)$ and $X/N(W,J)$ is a $K(N(A,J),1)$: here $K(G,1)$ means a path-connected space whose fundamental group is isomorphic to $G$ and whose homotopy groups in all degrees at least two vanish. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication.

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ the standard projection, and $W_J,A_J$ the standard parabolic subgroups generated by $J$. Put $N=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$. Let $\mathcal D$ be the relative arrangement groupoid, $\mathcal R$ the reduced ribbon groupoid, $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ the crossing-to-ribbon functor and $\mathcal Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/N$ the orbit functor. A vertex group is the group of arrows from a specified object to itself. Write $d=(e,J)$, $\mathcal D_J=\mathcal D_d$ and $\mathcal R_J$ for the vertex group of $\mathcal R$ at $J$.

Let $X$ be the relative complexified arrangement complement, $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$ the equivariant equivalence, $x=p(d)$ and $\bar x$ the image of $x$ in $X/N$. With first-path-first products and ordinary composition of deck transformations, the exact sequence $1\to\mathcal D_J\xrightarrow{\mathcal Q}(\mathcal D/N)_{\mathcal Qd}\to N\to1$ is isomorphic, with identity on $N$, to the topological covering sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)\to N\to1$. It is also isomorphic, with identity on $\mathcal D_J$ and $N$, to $1\to\mathcal D_J\xrightarrow{\mathcal G}\mathcal R_J\xrightarrow{\psi}N\to1$.

For $\mu\in\mathcal R_J$, its unique $\mathcal G$-lift from $d$ ends at $(\pi(\mu),J)$; in particular $\pi(\mu)$ is the minimum-length representative of its right $W_J$-coset and $\psi(\mu)=\pi(\mu)W_J$. Under the isomorphism $\mathcal R_J\cong N(A,J)$ induced by quotienting by $A_J$, $\psi$ agrees with the map $\overline\pi:N(A,J)\to N$ induced by $\pi$.

More explicitly, let $q_J:\mathcal R_J\to N(A,J)$ be the quotient isomorphism, let $\mathcal G':\mathcal D/N\to\mathcal R$ be the isomorphism with $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'\mathcal Q$, and let $\bar p:\mathcal D/N\to\Pi_1(X/N)$ be induced by $p$. Write $p_d$, $\bar p_{\mathcal Qd}$ and $\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd}$ for the induced vertex-group maps. The comparison from the $\mathcal Q$-sequence to the topological sequence has components $(p_d,\bar p_{\mathcal Qd},\mathrm{id}_N)$; the comparison from the $\mathcal Q$-sequence to the ribbon sequence has components $(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D_J},\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd},\mathrm{id}_N)$. Consequently the resulting algebraic-to-topological comparison has middle map $\Phi=\bar p_{\mathcal Qd}\circ(\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd})^{-1}\circ q_J^{-1}:N(A,J)\to\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)$.

article.source_excerpt:
3.5. The Deligne groupoid. The Deligne groupoid was introduced in [9] to study the topology
of finite simplicial arrangements (and prove the K(π, 1) conjecture for finite real reflection groups).
Although our setting is more general than that of Deligne, the construction of the Deligne groupoid
can be carried out similarly. However, the key features proven by Deligne, namely that the Deligne
groupoid is a Garside groupoid equivalent to the fundamental groupoid of the complexified com-
plement, only hold (to our knowledge) in the setting of finite simplicial arrangements.
  To the locally-finite arrangement (Cone(J)◦, HJ), we associate an oriented graph on the set
of vertices Cham(J). To every pair of adjacent chambers we associate a 2-cycle, i.e. given two
adjacent chambers (x, I) and (y, K) there is one arrow (x, I) →(y, K) and another opposite arrow
(y, K) →(x, I). We continue to use the notation ωa,I as above to label these arrows.
 A path in this graph from (x, I) to (y, K) is a geodesic if it is a path of minimal length between
(x, I) and (y, K). Equivalently, it crosses every hyperplane H ∈HJ at most once.
  Define D+ := D+(J) as the category with:
     • objects given by Cham(J); and
     • morphisms HomD+((x, I), (y, K)) are paths from (x, I) to (y, K) modulo the relation gen-
       erated by the identification of any two geodesic paths with the same source and target.
The arrangement groupoid D := D(J) associated to (Cone(J)◦, HJ) is defined as the groupoid
completion of D+.  If Γ is of spherical-type, then (Cone(J)◦, HJ) = (ΘJ, HJ) is a finite simplicial
arrangement, and we call D the Deligne groupoid. In this case, D is equivalent to the fundamental
            C             C
groupoid of XJ , denoted π1(X J ) [9].

alphabeta.original_label: Deligne asphericity used for the relative complement
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let $\mathcal H$ be a finite collection of linear hyperplanes. Suppose every chamber, meaning every connected component of $V\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}H$, is an open simplicial cone: it is the image of an open positive orthant under a linear isomorphism onto $V$. Write $V_{\mathbb C}=V\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, with complex scalar multiplication $z\cdot(v\otimes w)=v\otimes zw$ and its finite-dimensional Euclidean topology. Then the complexified complement $M=V_{\mathbb C}\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H}(H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$ is nonempty and path-connected, admits a CW structure, and has vanishing homotopy groups in all degrees at least two. Choose a vertex $b$ of such a CW structure and put $\pi=\pi_1(M,b)$. With the identity identification of this fundamental group with $\pi$, the based space $(M,b)$ is a $K(\pi,1)$. Here a $K(\pi,1)$ means a connected based CW complex with a specified fundamental-group isomorphism to $\pi$ and vanishing higher homotopy groups; the latter vanishing is called asphericity.

In particular, let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with $W$ finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. For its relative space $\Theta_J$, relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$ and relative complexified complement $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$, the space $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ admits a CW structure and, after choosing a vertex basepoint, is a $K(\pi,1)$ for its own fundamental group with the identity identification.

alphabeta.original_label: Spherical relative arrangements and Deligne topology
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system, let $J\subseteq S$, and use its relative space $\Theta_J$, relative cone $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$, relative hyperplanes $\mathcal H^J$, positive arrangement category $\mathcal D^+(J)$ and groupoid completion $\mathcal D(J)$. Suppose $W$ is finite, also called spherical type. Then $\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ=\Theta_J$, and $(\Theta_J,\mathcal H^J)$ is a finite central simplicial arrangement: its hyperplanes are finite in number, pass through the origin, and each chamber is a linear image of an open positive orthant in $\Theta_J$.

The category $\mathcal D^+(J)$ has a finite-type atomic categorical Garside structure. Thus its completion $\mathcal D(J)$ is a Garside groupoid in the sense of being the groupoid completion of that Garside category. It is equivalent to the fundamental groupoid $\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C})$ of the relative complexified complement. These deductions use the finite simplicial hypotheses; no extension to a general nonsimplicial or infinite arrangement is asserted.

alphabeta.original_label: Spherical normaliser quotient classifying spaces
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group and $P$ the kernel of its standard projection to $W$. For $G=W,A$, let $G_J$ be the standard parabolic subgroup generated by the generators indexed by $J$, and put $N(G,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)/G_J$, where the normaliser consists of the elements conjugating $G_J$ to itself. Let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$.

Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified hyperplane complement. The induced action of $N(W,J)$ gives a quotient $X/N(W,J)$. Then $X$ is a $K(N(P,J),1)$ and $X/N(W,J)$ is a $K(N(A,J),1)$. Here $K(G,1)$ means a path-connected space whose fundamental group is isomorphic to $G$ and whose homotopy groups in all degrees at least two vanish.

alphabeta.original_label: Main spherical theorem combining exact sequences and asphericity
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $S$ is finite and $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ its standard projection, and $P=\ker\pi$. For $G=W,A$, let $G_J$ be the subgroup generated by the standard generators indexed by $J$, and define $N(G,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)/G_J$, where $\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)=\{g\in G:gG_Jg^{-1}=G_J\}$. Let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$.

Let $\Theta_J$ be the subspace of the real dual reflection representation on which the simple roots indexed by $J$ vanish, and let $\mathcal H^J$ consist of the distinct hyperplanes obtained by restricting to $\Theta_J$ those root hyperplanes that do not contain it. In spherical type, the relative complexified complement is $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}=(\Theta_J\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}(H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$, with its subspace topology. The action of $N(W,J)$ on $X$ is the complex-linear extension of $(nW_J)\cdot f=nf$, where $(nf)(v)=f(n^{-1}v)$ for $f\in\Theta_J$, $v$ in the real root space and $n\in\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)$. It is independent of the representative and preserves $X$. For $x\in X$, let $\bar x$ be its image in $X/N(W,J)$ under this action.

The algebraic exact sequence $1\to N(P,J)\to N(A,J)\to N(W,J)\to1$ is isomorphic to the covering exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)\to N(W,J)\to1$, with the identity on $N(W,J)$. In particular, $N(P,J)\cong\pi_1(X,x)$ and $N(A,J)\cong\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)$. Moreover, $X$ is a $K(N(P,J),1)$ and $X/N(W,J)$ is a $K(N(A,J),1)$: here $K(G,1)$ means a path-connected space whose fundamental group is isomorphic to $G$ and whose homotopy groups in all degrees at least two vanish. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication.

alphabeta.original_label: Relative free action, normal cover and exact sequence
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system and $J\subseteq S$. Write $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and let $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified complement of [def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers). The induced diagonal $N(W,J)$-action on $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ is free and properly discontinuous: every point has an open neighbourhood disjoint from all its nonidentity translates.

The quotient map is a normal covering, meaning a covering whose deck transformations act transitively on every fibre. For $x\in\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ and its image $\overline x$, it induces the exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C},x)\to\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}/N(W,J),\overline x)\to N(W,J)\to1$. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication; the last map sends a loop to the unique element taking $x$ to the endpoint of its lift starting at $x$.

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with vertex set $\Gamma_0$ and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. The chamber-label set $\mathrm{Cham}(J)$ consists of the pairs $(x,I)$ such that $W_Jx=xW_I$ and $x$ has minimum length in $xW_I$. Write $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ for the normaliser quotient.

alphabeta.original_label: Relative free action, normal cover and exact sequence
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system and $J\subseteq S$. Write $N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and let $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified complement of [def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-relative-complement-artin-tits-normalisers). The induced diagonal $N(W,J)$-action on $\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ is free and properly discontinuous: every point has an open neighbourhood disjoint from all its nonidentity translates.

The quotient map is a normal covering, meaning a covering whose deck transformations act transitively on every fibre. For $x\in\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ and its image $\overline x$, it induces the exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C},x)\to\pi_1(\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}/N(W,J),\overline x)\to N(W,J)\to1$. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication; the last map sends a loop to the unique element taking $x$ to the endpoint of its lift starting at $x$.

h1_values: Relative free action, normal cover and exact sequence

article.source_excerpt:
Definition 5.1 ([17]). Let Γ be a spherical Coxeter diagram and let J be a subset of the vertex
set Γ0. The ribbon groupoid R′ := R′(J) associated to J is defined as follows.
     • The objects are the subsets of Γ0 which are associates of J (see Definition 2.7).
     • HomR′(I, K) := {β ∈A | A+I β = βA+K}. Here A+I  is the submonoid of AI generated by the
        σi for i ∈I. Composition is given by multiplication in A (on the right).

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, with vertex set $\Gamma_0$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group, with generators $\sigma_i$ indexed by $i\in\Gamma_0$, and let $A_I^+$ be the submonoid generated by the $\sigma_i$ for $i\in I$. Fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. An associate of $J$ is a subset $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$ whose standard Coxeter parabolic subgroup $W_I=\langle s_i:i\in I\rangle$ is conjugate to $W_J$ in $W$.

The **ribbon groupoid** $\mathcal R'(J)$ has the associates of $J$ as objects. For associates $I,K$, its arrows $I\to K$ are tagged by source and target and have labels

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal R'(J)}(I,K)=\{\beta\in A:A_I^+\beta=\beta A_K^+\}.$$

Here equality is equality of subsets of $A$. For $\beta:I\to K$ and $\gamma:K\to L$, their composite, read left to right, has label $\beta\gamma$. The identity at $I$ has label $1\in A$.

article.source_excerpt:
Definition 5.1 ([17]). Let Γ be a spherical Coxeter diagram and let J be a subset of the vertex
set Γ0. The ribbon groupoid R′ := R′(J) associated to J is defined as follows.
     • The objects are the subsets of Γ0 which are associates of J (see Definition 2.7).
     • HomR′(I, K) := {β ∈A | A+I β = βA+K}. Here A+I  is the submonoid of AI generated by the
        σi for i ∈I. Composition is given by multiplication in A (on the right).

alphabeta.original_label: Positive Artin and parabolic monoids
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank Coxeter system with $S=\{s_i:i\in\Gamma_0\}$, let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group with Artin generators $\sigma_i$, and let $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$. Write $A_I$ for the standard parabolic subgroup generated by the $\sigma_i$ with $i\in I$.

A **monoid** is a set with an associative binary operation and a two-sided identity. A **submonoid** of a monoid is a subset containing the identity and closed under the operation. The **positive Artin submonoid** $A^+$ is the submonoid of $A$ generated by all its Artin generators: explicitly, it consists of all finite products $\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_n}$ with $n\geq 0$ and $i_k\in\Gamma_0$. The **positive parabolic submonoid** $A_I^+$ is the submonoid of $A_I$ generated by $\{\sigma_i:i\in I\}$: explicitly, it consists of the same finite products with every $i_k\in I$. In both cases the empty product is the identity of $A$.

These definitions do not require spherical type, meaning that $W$ is finite. The article imposes spherical type in Sections 5 and 6.

alphabeta.original_label: Positive elementary ribbon elements
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, with vertex set $\Gamma_0$ and associated Artin–Tits group $A$. Let $A^+$ be the submonoid of $A$ generated by the standard Artin generators. For $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$, let $w_J$ be the longest element of the standard parabolic subgroup $W_J$, and let $\Delta_J$ be its positive reduced-word lift in $A$.

Let $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$ and $a\in I^c=\Gamma_0\setminus I$. Write $I+a=I\cup\{a\}$, and let $[I,a]$ be the vertex set of the connected component containing $a$ in the diagram induced on $I+a$. Write $[I,a]-a=[I,a]\setminus\{a\}$. The **positive elementary ribbon element** associated to $(a,I)$ is

$$\mu_{a,I}=\Delta_{[I,a]-a}^{-1}\Delta_{[I,a]}\in A^+.$$

Equivalently, $\mu_{a,I}=\Delta_I^{-1}\Delta_{I+a}$. Inverses and products in these expressions are taken in $A$.

h1_values: Positive elementary ribbon elements

alphabeta.original_label: Reduced ribbon groupoid
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, with vertex set $\Gamma_0$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. For $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$, write $W_I$ for the subgroup generated by the simple reflections indexed by $I$. An **associate** of $J$ is a subset $I$ for which $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$ in $W$.

Let $\mathcal R'(J)$ be the ribbon groupoid: its objects are the associates of $J$, and an arrow $I\to K$ is an element $\beta\in A$ with $A_I^+\beta=\beta A_K^+$, tagged with its source and target. Here $A_I^+$ is the submonoid generated by the standard Artin generators indexed by $I$. Composition is multiplication from left to right.

For an associate $I$ and $a\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$, put $T=I\cup\{a\}$. Let $w_T$ be the longest element of $W_T$, let $\iota_T:T\to T$ be the opposition permutation defined by $w_T\alpha_i=-\alpha_{\iota_T(i)}$ on the simple roots, and put $K=T\setminus\{\iota_T(a)\}$. If $\Delta_L$ denotes the positive reduced-word lift in $A$ of the longest element of $W_L$, the elementary ribbon is $\mu_{a,I}=\Delta_I^{-1}\Delta_T$, regarded as an arrow $I\to K$ of $\mathcal R'(J)$.

The **reduced ribbon groupoid** $\mathcal R(J)$ is the subgroupoid of $\mathcal R'(J)$ with all the same objects whose arrows are finite composable products of the arrows $\mu_{a,I}$ and their inverses, including empty products as identities. Equivalently, it is the smallest subgroupoid of $\mathcal R'(J)$ containing every object and every such elementary ribbon arrow.

alphabeta.original_label: Spherical Artin normaliser splitting
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, and let $J$ be a subset of its vertex set. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group and $A_J$ its standard parabolic subgroup. Let $\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid, and write $\mathcal R_J$ for its vertex group at $J$, consisting of its arrows from $J$ to $J$ under composition.

The normaliser $\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ is the internal semidirect product $A_J\rtimes\mathcal R_J$: each normaliser element has a unique expression $pr$ with $p\in A_J$ and $r\in\mathcal R_J$. Consequently the quotient homomorphism restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal R_J\cong N(A,J)$, where $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$.

a product of generating morphisms:

alphabeta.original_label: Two ribbon-lcm expressions and presentation
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram with vertex set $S$, let $A^+$ be its positive Artin monoid, and fix $J\subseteq S$. Use the reduced ribbon groupoid $\mathcal R(J)$ and elementary arrows $\mu_{a,I}=\Delta_I^{-1}\Delta_{I\cup\{a\}}:I\to K$ of [def-reduced-ribbon-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-reduced-ribbon-artin-tits-normalisers), where $I$ ranges over the associates of $J$ and $a\in S\setminus I$. Thus an associate means a subset whose standard parabolic Coxeter subgroup is conjugate to that of $J$.

For distinct $a,b\in S\setminus I$, the least common multiple $\mu_{a,I}\vee\mu_{b,I}$ for left divisibility in $A^+$ is represented by a morphism of $\mathcal R(J)$ with source $I$. It has exactly two expressions as composable products of elementary arrows: one begins with $\mu_{a,I}$ and the other with $\mu_{b,I}$. If their lengths are $m$ and $n$, respectively, these expressions have the form $\mu_{a_1,I_1}\cdots\mu_{a_m,I_m}$ and $\mu_{b_1,L_1}\cdots\mu_{b_n,L_n}$, with $a_1=a$, $b_1=b$, and $I_1=L_1=I$.

The elementary arrows, their formal inverses, and the groupoid identity and inverse laws generate $\mathcal R(J)$, and the equalities between these two expressions, over all associates $I$ and all distinct pairs $a,b\in S\setminus I$, give a complete set of defining relations. For $a=b$, the lcm is $\mu_{a,I}$ and has one elementary-arrow expression; the corresponding equality is tautological.

Moreover $q$ is the join of $v_{a,I}$ and $v_{b,I}$ in the prefix weak order: $u\leq v$ means $v=ux$ with $\ell(v)=\ell(u)+\ell(x)$. This is the order called weak left Bruhat order in the article.

For $a=b$, the lcm is $\mu_{a,I}$ and the join is $v_{a,I}$; the assertion of two distinct expressions is not made in this case.

alphabeta.original_label: Reduced ribbon groupoid
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, with vertex set $\Gamma_0$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. For $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$, write $W_I$ for the subgroup generated by the simple reflections indexed by $I$. An **associate** of $J$ is a subset $I$ for which $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$ in $W$.

Let $\mathcal R'(J)$ be the ribbon groupoid: its objects are the associates of $J$, and an arrow $I\to K$ is an element $\beta\in A$ with $A_I^+\beta=\beta A_K^+$, tagged with its source and target. Here $A_I^+$ is the submonoid generated by the standard Artin generators indexed by $I$. Composition is multiplication from left to right.

For an associate $I$ and $a\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$, put $T=I\cup\{a\}$. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, and let $J$ be a subset of its vertex set. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group and $A_J$ its standard parabolic subgroup. Let $\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid, and write $\mathcal R_J$ for its vertex group at $J$, consisting of its arrows from $J$ to $J$ under composition.

The normaliser $\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ is the internal semidirect product $A_J\rtimes\mathcal R_J$: each normaliser element has a unique expression $pr$ with $p\in A_J$ and $r\in\mathcal R_J$. Consequently the quotient homomorphism restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal R_J\cong N(A,J)$, where $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$.

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with $S=\{s_i:i\in\Gamma_0\}$, length $\ell$, and simple roots $\alpha_i$ in its standard geometric representation. Let $A$ be the Artin–Tits group with generators $\sigma_i$, and for $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$ write $W_J=\langle s_j:j\in J\rangle$ and $A_J=\langle\sigma_j:j\in J\rangle$. Suppose that $W_J$ is finite.

The **longest element** $w_J$ is the unique element of $W_J$ whose $\ell$-length is maximal. Its **positive lift** is $\Delta_J=\sigma_{w_J}\in A_J$: if $w_J=s_{j_1}\cdots s_{j_r}$ is a shortest expression in simple generators, set $\sigma_{w_J}=\sigma_{j_1}\cdots\sigma_{j_r}$, with the empty product equal to the identity. The **opposition permutation** $\iota_J:J\to J$ is the unique permutation satisfying $w_J\alpha_j=-\alpha_{\iota_J(j)}$ for every $j\in J$.

article.source_excerpt:
Definition 5.5 ([17]). Let Γ be a spherical Coxeter diagram, and let J be a subset of the vertex set
Γ0. The reduced ribbon groupoid R := R(J) associated to J is the subgroupoid of the ribbon
groupoid R′ whose objects coincide with the objects of R′, and whose morphisms are generated
by the morphisms µa,I for I an associate of J and a ∈Ic.
limits: Literal subgroup loops and categorical End have different multiplication orders; retain the explicit opposite bridge.
Article credits Theorem5.6 to [14, Proposition4.4]; this is author attribution, distinct from actual Lean suppliers.

article.source_excerpt:
Theorem 5.6 ([14, Proposition 4.4]). Let Γ be a spherical Coxeter diagram with associated Artin–
Tits group A, and let J be a subset of the vertex set Γ0.  Let R be the reduced ribbon groupoid
associated to J. There is an isomorphism of groups

alphabeta.original_label: Reduced ribbon groupoid
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, with vertex set $\Gamma_0$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group and fix $J\subseteq\Gamma_0$. For $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$, write $W_I$ for the subgroup generated by the simple reflections indexed by $I$. An **associate** of $J$ is a subset $I$ for which $W_I$ is conjugate to $W_J$ in $W$.

Let $\mathcal R'(J)$ be the ribbon groupoid: its objects are the associates of $J$, and an arrow $I\to K$ is an element $\beta\in A$ with $A_I^+\beta=\beta A_K^+$, tagged with its source and target. Here $A_I^+$ is the submonoid generated by the standard Artin generators indexed by $I$. Composition is multiplication from left to right.

For an associate $I$ and $a\in\Gamma_0\setminus I$, put $T=I\cup\{a\}$. Let $w_T$ be the longest element of $W_T$, let $\iota_T:T\to T$ be the opposition permutation defined by $w_T\alpha_i=-\alpha_{\iota_T(i)}$ on the simple roots, and put $K=T\setminus\{\iota_T(a)\}$. If $\Delta_L$ denotes the positive reduced-word lift in $A$ of the longest element of $W_L$, the elementary ribbon is $\mu_{a,I}=\Delta_I^{-1}\Delta_T$, regarded as an arrow $I\to K$ of $\mathcal R'(J)$.

The **reduced ribbon groupoid** $\mathcal R(J)$ is the subgroupoid of $\mathcal R'(J)$ with all the same objects whose arrows are finite composable products of the arrows $\mu_{a,I}$ and their inverses, including empty products as identities. Equivalently, it is the smallest subgroupoid of $\mathcal R'(J)$ containing every object and every such elementary ribbon arrow.

alphabeta.original_label: Spherical Artin normaliser splitting
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter diagram, meaning that its Coxeter group $W$ is finite, and let $J$ be a subset of its vertex set. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group and $A_J$ its standard parabolic subgroup. Let $\mathcal R(J)$ be the reduced ribbon groupoid, and write $\mathcal R_J$ for its vertex group at $J$, consisting of its arrows from $J$ to $J$ under composition.

The normaliser $\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ is the internal semidirect product $A_J\rtimes\mathcal R_J$: each normaliser element has a unique expression $pr$ with $p\in A_J$ and $r\in\mathcal R_J$. Consequently the quotient homomorphism restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal R_J\cong N(A,J)$, where $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$.

alphabeta.original_label: Isomorphism of algebraic and topological normaliser sequences
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group, let $\pi:A\to W$ be its standard projection and let $P=\ker\pi$. Write $W_J$ and $A_J$ for the subgroups generated by the standard generators indexed by $J$. For $G=W,A$, put $N(G,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)/G_J$, where $\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)=\{g\in G:gG_Jg^{-1}=G_J\}$. Let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$.

Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified hyperplane complement, let $x\in X$, and let $\bar x$ be its image in $X/N(W,J)$. The algebraic exact sequence $1\to N(P,J)\to N(A,J)\xrightarrow{\bar\pi}N(W,J)\to1$ is isomorphic to the covering exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)\to N(W,J)\to1$, with the identity on $N(W,J)$. In particular, $N(P,J)\cong\pi_1(X,x)$ and $N(A,J)\cong\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)$. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication.

alphabeta.original_label: Intermediate exact sequences and deck morphism in Theorem 6.7
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ the standard projection, and $W_J,A_J$ the standard parabolic subgroups generated by $J$. Put $N=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$. Let $\mathcal D$ be the relative arrangement groupoid, $\mathcal R$ the reduced ribbon groupoid, $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ the crossing-to-ribbon functor and $\mathcal Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/N$ the orbit functor. A vertex group is the group of arrows from a specified object to itself. Write $d=(e,J)$, $\mathcal D_J=\mathcal D_d$ and $\mathcal R_J$ for the vertex group of $\mathcal R$ at $J$.

Let $X$ be the relative complexified arrangement complement, $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$ the equivariant equivalence, $x=p(d)$ and $\bar x$ the image of $x$ in $X/N$. With first-path-first products and ordinary composition of deck transformations, the exact sequence $1\to\mathcal D_J\xrightarrow{\mathcal Q}(\mathcal D/N)_{\mathcal Qd}\to N\to1$ is isomorphic, with identity on $N$, to the topological covering sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)\to N\to1$. It is also isomorphic, with identity on $\mathcal D_J$ and $N$, to $1\to\mathcal D_J\xrightarrow{\mathcal G}\mathcal R_J\xrightarrow{\psi}N\to1$.

For $\mu\in\mathcal R_J$, its unique $\mathcal G$-lift from $d$ ends at $(\pi(\mu),J)$; in particular $\pi(\mu)$ is the minimum-length representative of its right $W_J$-coset and $\psi(\mu)=\pi(\mu)W_J$. Under the isomorphism $\mathcal R_J\cong N(A,J)$ induced by quotienting by $A_J$, $\psi$ agrees with the map $\overline\pi:N(A,J)\to N$ induced by $\pi$.

More explicitly, let $q_J:\mathcal R_J\to N(A,J)$ be the quotient isomorphism, let $\mathcal G':\mathcal D/N\to\mathcal R$ be the isomorphism with $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'\mathcal Q$, and let $\bar p:\mathcal D/N\to\Pi_1(X/N)$ be induced by $p$. Write $p_d$, $\bar p_{\mathcal Qd}$ and $\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd}$ for the induced vertex-group maps. The comparison from the $\mathcal Q$-sequence to the topological sequence has components $(p_d,\bar p_{\mathcal Qd},\mathrm{id}_N)$; the comparison from the $\mathcal Q$-sequence to the ribbon sequence has components $(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D_J},\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd},\mathrm{id}_N)$. Consequently the resulting algebraic-to-topological comparison has middle map $\Phi=\bar p_{\mathcal Qd}\circ(\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd})^{-1}\circ q_J^{-1}:N(A,J)\to\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)$.

alphabeta.original_label: Isomorphism of algebraic and topological normaliser sequences
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, meaning that $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be the associated Artin–Tits group, let $\pi:A\to W$ be its standard projection and let $P=\ker\pi$. Write $W_J$ and $A_J$ for the subgroups generated by the standard generators indexed by $J$. For $G=W,A$, put $N(G,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)/G_J$, where $\operatorname{Norm}_G(G_J)=\{g\in G:gG_Jg^{-1}=G_J\}$. Let $N(P,J)$ be the image of $P\cap\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)$ in $N(A,J)$.

Let $X=\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}$ be the relative complexified hyperplane complement, let $x\in X$, and let $\bar x$ be its image in $X/N(W,J)$. The algebraic exact sequence $1\to N(P,J)\to N(A,J)\xrightarrow{\bar\pi}N(W,J)\to1$ is isomorphic to the covering exact sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)\to N(W,J)\to1$, with the identity on $N(W,J)$. In particular, $N(P,J)\cong\pi_1(X,x)$ and $N(A,J)\cong\pi_1(X/N(W,J),\bar x)$. Fundamental groups use first-path-first multiplication.

alphabeta.original_label: Intermediate exact sequences and deck morphism in Theorem 6.7
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(W,S)$ be a finite-rank spherical Coxeter system, so $W$ is finite, and let $J\subseteq S$. Let $A$ be its Artin–Tits group, $\pi:A\to W$ the standard projection, and $W_J,A_J$ the standard parabolic subgroups generated by $J$. Put $N=N(W,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_W(W_J)/W_J$ and $N(A,J)=\operatorname{Norm}_A(A_J)/A_J$. Let $\mathcal D$ be the relative arrangement groupoid, $\mathcal R$ the reduced ribbon groupoid, $\mathcal G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal R$ the crossing-to-ribbon functor and $\mathcal Q:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D/N$ the orbit functor. A vertex group is the group of arrows from a specified object to itself. Write $d=(e,J)$, $\mathcal D_J=\mathcal D_d$ and $\mathcal R_J$ for the vertex group of $\mathcal R$ at $J$.

Let $X$ be the relative complexified arrangement complement, $p:\mathcal D\to\Pi_1(X)$ the equivariant equivalence, $x=p(d)$ and $\bar x$ the image of $x$ in $X/N$. With first-path-first products and ordinary composition of deck transformations, the exact sequence $1\to\mathcal D_J\xrightarrow{\mathcal Q}(\mathcal D/N)_{\mathcal Qd}\to N\to1$ is isomorphic, with identity on $N$, to the topological covering sequence $1\to\pi_1(X,x)\to\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)\to N\to1$. It is also isomorphic, with identity on $\mathcal D_J$ and $N$, to $1\to\mathcal D_J\xrightarrow{\mathcal G}\mathcal R_J\xrightarrow{\psi}N\to1$.

For $\mu\in\mathcal R_J$, its unique $\mathcal G$-lift from $d$ ends at $(\pi(\mu),J)$; in particular $\pi(\mu)$ is the minimum-length representative of its right $W_J$-coset and $\psi(\mu)=\pi(\mu)W_J$. Under the isomorphism $\mathcal R_J\cong N(A,J)$ induced by quotienting by $A_J$, $\psi$ agrees with the map $\overline\pi:N(A,J)\to N$ induced by $\pi$.

More explicitly, let $q_J:\mathcal R_J\to N(A,J)$ be the quotient isomorphism, let $\mathcal G':\mathcal D/N\to\mathcal R$ be the isomorphism with $\mathcal G=\mathcal G'\mathcal Q$, and let $\bar p:\mathcal D/N\to\Pi_1(X/N)$ be induced by $p$. Write $p_d$, $\bar p_{\mathcal Qd}$ and $\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd}$ for the induced vertex-group maps. The comparison from the $\mathcal Q$-sequence to the topological sequence has components $(p_d,\bar p_{\mathcal Qd},\mathrm{id}_N)$; the comparison from the $\mathcal Q$-sequence to the ribbon sequence has components $(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D_J},\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd},\mathrm{id}_N)$. Consequently the resulting algebraic-to-topological comparison has middle map $\Phi=\bar p_{\mathcal Qd}\circ(\mathcal G'_{\mathcal Qd})^{-1}\circ q_J^{-1}:N(A,J)\to\pi_1(X/N,\bar x)$.

alphabeta.original_label: Relative complexified hyperplane complement
alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system with finite $S$, and let $J\subseteq S$. In the real dual representation space $\Theta$, let $\Theta_J$ be the subspace on which the simple roots indexed by $J$ vanish. Let $\mathrm{Cone}(J)$ be the intersection of the Tits cone with $\Theta_J$, and let $\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ$ be its interior in $\Theta_J$. Let $\mathcal H^J$ be the set of distinct hyperplanes obtained by restricting to $\Theta_J$ those root hyperplanes that do not contain $\Theta_J$.

The **relative complexified hyperplane complement** is the space

$$\mathcal X_J^{\mathbb C}=(\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ\times\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ)\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}(H\times H).$$

It has the subspace topology inherited from the product topology. If $W$ is finite, a case also called **spherical type**, then $\mathrm{Cone}(J)^\circ=\Theta_J$. Under the real-linear identification $(x,y)\mapsto x\otimes1+y\otimes i$ of $\Theta_J\times\Theta_J$ with $\Theta_J\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, the space is

$$(\Theta_J\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)\setminus\bigcup_{H\in\mathcal H^J}(H\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C).$$

alphabeta.source_excerpt:
Use the Coxeter-system notation of [def-coxeter-data-artin-tits-normalisers](item-def-coxeter-data-artin-tits-normalisers): $\Gamma_0$ is the vertex set, $V=\bigoplus_{i\in\Gamma_0}\mathbb R\alpha_i$ has basis $(\alpha_i)_{i\in\Gamma_0}$, and $\Theta=V^*$ is the space of real linear functionals on $V$. The vertex set may be infinite.

For $I\subseteq\Gamma_0$, write $I^c=\Gamma_0\setminus I$. Define the parabolic coordinate subspace $\Theta_I$ and the fundamental face $C_I$ by $\Theta_I=\{\varphi\in\Theta:\varphi(\alpha_i)=0\text{ for every }i\in I\}$ and $C_I=\{\varphi\in\Theta_I:\varphi(\alpha_j)>0\text{ for every }j\in I^c\}$.
